chunks: He said: Ali ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Zur'ah ibn Muhammad from al-Mufaddal, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Soon the Banu al-Abbas will meddle with this son of mine, but they will never reach him. Then he said: Nor will there be a mourner who mourns for him, nor an official who takes him away, nor an inheritance to be distributed, nor a slave girl to be sold.

key_terms.سَائِقَةٌ: an official/capturer who takes him away

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq predict about the fate of his son Musa al-Kadhim regarding the Banu Abbas?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the unique eschatological status of Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.), distinguishing his death from typical worldly transitions by noting the absence of standard mourning rituals, captors, or inheritance division. It serves as a key evidence for the Waqifiya refutation, emphasizing that his departure was a divine mystery rather than a political execution or natural death with conventional social aftermath. The prediction underscores the Imam’s distinct spiritual authority and the hidden nature of his final moments, aligning with the concept of *ghayba* (occultation) in Shia thought.
